ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs and shareholders against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Community sanctions under Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and related regulations, French domestic assets-freezing measures of the Direction générale du Trésor, and Tracfin financial-intelligence reports. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for Politically Exposed Persons as defined by Articles L.561-10 and R.561-18 CMF, including foreign PEPs, their family members, and known close associates. Screening must be documented and retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (Registre National des Entreprises); name-search availability is checked on data.inpi.fr.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS name may be stated in any language using Latin characters, but the official French register will enter it as it appears in the statuts. If a foreign-language name is selected, a sworn French transliteration or translation must be included in the statutes. The legal form designation 'SAS' must always accompany the business name. The name must not be contrary to public order or good morals and must not mislead the public as to the company's object.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a formal name-reservation deposit. A name-clearance result is represented by the order number of the draft statutes checked through data.inpi.fr and is treated as commercially valid for a 30-day window. If the proposed SAS name conflicts with an existing registered entity or protected intellectual property right, the formalities centre issues a rejection. Within one month, the incorporating attorney may file a written administrative complaint with the INPI formalities service for reconsideration, or resubmit amended statutes after removing the conflicting token. In parallel, an opposition action may be brought before the Tribunal judiciaire against the prior mark or trade name. Because registration occurs at filing, an administrative appeal lies only against the INPI decision refusing to record the corporate name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) authorised by the prefecture of the department where the registered office is located. For a payment-service-entity license, virtual-office-only arrangements are not sufficient: ACPR and Tracfin expect a physical principal establishment with the actual management seat, compliant data-access infrastructure, AML records, and economic substance commensurate with the licensed activity. A virtual office may be used for mail forwarding only upon full disclosure to the ACPR and to the beneficial-owner register.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: unannounced on-site inspections by the ACPR, Tracfin, and the DGCCRF are a standard supervisory tool for licensed PSPs. Quantified risk of a physical inspection during the first licensing cycle is estimated at 70% or higher, as the license application triggers on-site verification of client onboarding, AML, KYC, and transaction-monitoring infrastructure within the first 12 months after incorporation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, through impots.gouv.fr and the applicable Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Customs export formalities are administered separately by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through the DELTA customs systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The filing generates the legal entity's SIREN and establishment SIRET identifiers through INSEE. The company then completes tax registration with the competent SIE and, where it conducts taxable transactions, requests a French VAT identification number. The VAT number normally has the format FR followed by a two-digit validation key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères using the prescribed registration forms and supporting documents, including constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identification of legal representatives, banking information, and evidence of French taxable transactions. The DGFiP may require a French tax representative for certain non-EU VAT refund or registration situations. Registration does not replace mandatory authorization as a payment institution, electronic-money institution, payment-service agent, or other regulated provider under the Monetary and Financial Code; such authorization is generally administered by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). There is no general U.S.-style check-the-box election. An eligible SAS may elect temporary taxation under the individual income tax regime under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for a maximum of five financial years, subject to statutory conditions including size limits, qualifying ownership, individual participation requirements, management conditions, and an operating business activity. The election is not generally available to a company whose shares are listed or whose activity is predominantly financial or asset-management based. A qualifying group may also elect French tax consolidation under the applicable group-regime provisions, subject to ownership and other statutory conditions. French and EU anti-hybrid mismatch rules under Articles 205 B et seq. of the French Tax Code operate as mandatory anti-abuse rules; they do not constitute an elective hybrid classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), administered under the French Tax Code and EU VAT rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the domestic franchise en base de TVA, the principal annual turnover threshold for services is EUR 37,500, with a higher tolerance threshold generally applicable under the statutory rules. The principal threshold for ordinary trading of goods is EUR 85,000. These thresholds are exemption thresholds, not a universal safe harbor from VAT registration. A non-established business may have to register from its first French taxable transaction, and the thresholds generally do not protect a business making transactions subject to reverse charge, importing goods, or otherwise requiring VAT reporting. B2B services supplied to a French business are often subject to customer reverse charge under the place-of-supply rules. Qualifying payment, transfer, and current-account transactions may be VAT-exempt under Article 261 C of the French Tax Code; technical, platform, data-processing, or administrative services are not automatically exempt merely because they support payment processing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and transaction-data reporting through accredited private platforms (Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires) connected to the public directory and the public invoicing platform. The current statutory timetable provides receipt capability for all French VAT-taxable businesses from 1 September 2026 and issuance obligations for large and intermediate businesses from 1 September 2026, with issuance obligations for small and medium-sized businesses and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to legally enacted transition changes. France does not operate a universal real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping model comparable to Italy's SDI for all invoices. Domestic B2B invoices must use structured electronic data containing the prescribed mandatory fields, and transaction and payment data may have to be transmitted through the designated platform. Cross-border B2B and B2C transactions are generally addressed through e-reporting rather than domestic B2B e-invoice transmission. Existing French invoice-content, record-retention, authenticity, integrity, and audit-trail requirements continue to apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from France or another EU Member State to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct, provided the supplier can substantiate export and satisfy the applicable invoicing and customs conditions. The evidence normally includes an electronically validated customs exit record or equivalent proof of exit, commercial documentation, transport evidence, and a consistent accounting trail. Services do not generally receive a domestic 0% export rate. B2B services supplied to a customer established outside France are normally governed by the place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT, subject to customer-status and evidence requirements. Certain qualifying financial and payment transactions are exempt under the specific French financial-services exemption, but technological or processing support services must be analyzed separately. VAT refunds require valid invoices, proof of taxable business use, and compliance with the applicable EU or non-EU refund procedure; non-established applicants may be subject to reciprocity, appointment of a tax representative, and filing deadlines.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration lodged through the applicable French/EU customs system, generally DELTA, with the Movement Reference Number and validated exit result or equivalent customs proof of exit
Commercial invoice, packing list where relevant, transport contract, and Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other transport evidence appropriate to the shipment
Proof that the goods were dispatched to a destination outside the EU and that the supplier, purchaser, or authorized intermediary satisfies the statutory export conditions
Import or destination-country customs evidence where reasonably required to corroborate delivery outside the EU
Accounting records linking the invoice, export declaration, transport evidence, and VAT return

Inward remittance evidence only where relevant to the commercial transaction or another applicable requirement; France does not generally require an Indian-style Inward Remittance Certificate as a universal condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days: Not applicable. France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for claiming export VAT exemption or VAT recovery. Export proceeds must nevertheless be recorded accurately, and payments remain subject to ordinary banking, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, accounting, and customs controls.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may deny the exemption or input-tax recovery and assess the VAT retrospectively where export, customer status, transport, payment-service qualification, or place-of-supply evidence is inadequate. Reassessed VAT is generally accompanied by late-payment interest, currently calculated under the applicable French statutory rate, and may attract a 10% surcharge for late payment, a 40% surcharge for deliberate failure, or an 80% surcharge for fraudulent conduct or abusive concealment, depending on the facts and procedural findings. False, fabricated, or knowingly misleading customs or tax documentation may also trigger customs sanctions, administrative fines, recovery of improperly refunded or unpaid VAT, and criminal exposure for tax fraud or related offenses. Payment-service activities incorrectly treated as VAT-exempt may result in output-VAT assessments, denial or apportionment of input-tax deductions, interest, and penalties for the full statutory assessment period, subject to limitation rules and fraud-related extensions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem, with prudential and payment-services supervision conducted by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), under the European Central Bank framework where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and applies the EU liberalized capital-movement regime. Current-account and capital-account payments are generally freely convertible and transferable without routine exchange-control approval. A French SAS may receive and remit foreign currency, dividends, shareholder loans, interest, royalties, and trade payments through regulated financial institutions. Profit remittance requires distributable accounting profits, approval of annual accounts and dividend allocation, compliance with corporate-law reserve requirements, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner and sanctions screening, and evidence that the payment is not a disguised capital distribution. Payment services and merchant-acquiring activity require authorization or registration under the French Monetary and Financial Code, generally through an ACPR-authorized payment institution, electronic-money institution, credit institution, or an appropriately structured agent arrangement. Client funds must be safeguarded and segregated from the company's operating funds; customer-money flows cannot be used to fund corporate liquidity. Cross-border transfers remain subject to AML, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax-reporting, transaction-monitoring, and beneficial-owner verification requirements. Foreign accounts held by French tax residents may trigger French tax reporting obligations, including annual account declarations where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may remain in euro or foreign-currency accounts and may be converted at the holder's discretion, subject to contractual bank terms, accounting, tax, AML, sanctions, and payment-services requirements. Export documentation, commercial invoices, customs evidence, merchant settlement reports, and reconciliation records should be retained to substantiate the commercial purpose and beneficial ownership of incoming funds. Banks may request transaction-purpose information and may apply internal reporting or enhanced due-diligence procedures. Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, high-risk customers, unusual routing, virtual assets, or unexplained third-party settlement may be delayed, rejected, or reported to Tracfin.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operating treasury and payment connectivity; Low to Medium for the core regulated PSP account structure. An offshore digital EMI cannot automatically provide regulated payment services in France. An EEA-authorized payment institution or electronic-money institution may passport services into France under PSD2 through the required notification process, while a non-EEA provider generally requires an appropriately authorized French or EEA entity, branch, agent, or banking partner. The SAS must verify the provider's authorization, safeguarding model, fund segregation, insolvency protection, settlement timetable, scheme access, safeguarding account location, data-processing arrangements, complaint handling, and termination rights. Offshore accounts do not remove French AML, sanctions, tax, accounting, PSD2, safeguarding, consumer-protection, or payment-institution obligations. A fintech account should not be used for client-money safeguarding unless the provider and account structure are legally capable of performing that function.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted following reliable electronic identification, video verification, qualified-signature procedures, and satisfactory documentary review. In practice, banks frequently require a live video interview or an in-person meeting for a newly incorporated SAS, a non-resident shareholder structure, a high-risk PSP, direct card-scheme activity, substantial cross-border flows, high-risk jurisdictions, complex beneficial ownership, or an application for safeguarding, acquiring, correspondent, or foreign-currency services. The bank may require certified or apostilled corporate documents, French translations, proof of registered office, proof of management address, tax-residency information, and evidence of regulatory authorization before activating accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The proposed business is described only as a payment gateway, merchant acquirer, clearing provider, or money-transmission business without a clear regulatory perimeter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ACPR authorization, registration, or passporting evidence; legal-perimeter memorandum; PSD2 service classification; regulatory business plan; flow-of-funds diagram; list of services and prohibited activities; safeguarding policy; AML-CFT framework; transaction-monitoring methodology; fraud and chargeback policy; card-scheme or sponsor-bank agreements; and board-approved compliance policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, offshore holding companies, trusts, or unexplained shareholder changes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the Registre national des entreprises; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart to natural persons; ultimate-beneficial-owner declarations; passports and proof of address for controllers; tax-residency self-certifications; source-of-wealth evidence; shareholder agreements; and certified corporate records for each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection or recurring inbound funds inconsistent with the stated business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; bank statements evidencing source of funds; audited or management accounts of the funder; tax returns where appropriate; investment agreement; capital-deposit certificate; purpose-of-payment narrative; expected monthly flow forecast; and reconciliation between injected capital, registered equity, and accounting records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected high-volume merchant flows, rapid pass-through activity, or commingling of customer funds with operating cash.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Separate operating and safeguarding account architecture; safeguarding-bank confirmation; daily reconciliation procedure; customer-money ledger; settlement waterfall; reserve and chargeback model; merchant onboarding policy; transaction limits; complaints and refund procedures; independent control testing; and written confirmation that customer funds are not used for corporate expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Merchants, customers, counterparties, or payment corridors connected with sanctioned, embargoed, high-risk, or secrecy jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Jurisdiction-risk matrix; sanctions-screening rules; customer and merchant due-diligence files; enhanced-due-diligence approvals; adverse-media screening; transaction-monitoring scenarios; prohibited-country list; escalation and blocking procedures; correspondent-bank controls; and documented legal review of each high-risk corridor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of virtual assets, payment intermediaries, nested accounts, third-party settlement, or unexplained correspondent-bank routing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete payment-flow map; counterparty register; contractual basis for each intermediary; wallet and virtual-asset risk controls where relevant; blockchain analytics methodology; source-and-destination-of-funds evidence; reconciliations; transaction purpose records; and senior-compliance approval for non-standard routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote directors, foreign management, virtual office, or lack of demonstrable French economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office agreement; lease or serviced-office evidence; French operational plan; employee and contractor records; director identification; management biographies; local compliance-officer appointment; board-meeting records; customer and vendor contracts; French tax registration; accounting engagement; and explanation of cross-border management arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence source of funds, source of wealth, expected transaction volumes, or commercial rationale for transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial model; first-year monthly cash-flow forecast; signed customer contracts; invoices and purchase orders; merchant-acquiring agreements; historical financial statements; tax filings; funding documents; bank statements; expected countries, currencies, counterparties, and payment purposes; and documented reconciliation controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed persons, fraud history, chargeback anomalies, or regulatory enforcement involving founders or counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent adverse-media analysis; PEP screening results; court and regulatory records; remediation evidence; compliance attestations; enhanced-due-diligence report; risk-acceptance memorandum; board approval; and documented ongoing-monitoring schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a regulated bank to the SAS's designated capital-deposit account before incorporation or to the corporate operating account after registration. Use the exact legal name of the SAS, registered address, French IBAN, BIC, and a payment narrative identifying the transaction as share capital subscription, share-premium contribution, or shareholder loan. France does not use a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary corporate capital transfers; the bank may instead request a transaction-purpose classification, underlying agreement, capital-deposit certificate, board or shareholder resolution, and supporting corporate records. The remitting bank and receiving bank should verify the originator, ultimate beneficiary, source of funds, beneficial owners, currency, intermediary banks, and sanctions status. For shareholder loans, document principal, maturity, interest, arm's-length terms, repayment waterfall, transfer-pricing support, and applicable withholding-tax treatment. Record the foreign-currency amount and euro value in the accounting ledger, reconcile bank statements to the capital register, and retain SWIFT messages and supporting documents. Where an international investment, regulated activity, or sector-specific filing is applicable, complete the relevant French or EU notification before or after funding as legally required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT MT103 or the current ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA cross-border payments. The payment file should contain the exact beneficiary name, IBAN or account number, BIC, invoice number, contract reference, purpose, currency, and ultimate beneficiary information. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, including confirmed or unconfirmed Commercial LCs, for higher-risk trade corridors, new counterparties, or document-controlled shipments. Banks may require commercial invoices, purchase orders, transport documents, customs declarations, insurance documents, sanctions screening, and proof of goods or services. For a PSP, merchant settlement must follow the contractual settlement cycle and safeguarding rules; operating-account payments must not be funded from safeguarded customer money. Fedwire is a US domestic clearing rail and is not a direct French rail; USD payments may access Fedwire through a US correspondent bank, with applicable intermediary-bank, sanctions, cut-off, and beneficiary-screening controls. Maintain payment approval segregation, dual authorization, beneficiary-change verification, daily bank reconciliation, failed-payment monitoring, and complete audit trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with an authorized bank or investment firm for forecast or committed commercial exposures, supported by a documented hedging policy, underlying exposure, maturity, counterparty limits, valuation controls, and accounting treatment.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for recurring funding, liquidity, or balance-sheet exposures, subject to contractual netting, collateral, counterparty-credit, valuation, and EMIR-related requirements where applicable.
FX options and option collars for asymmetric protection of forecast receipts or payments, subject to suitability, premium, valuation, accounting, and governance controls.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, provided the product is legally available to the entity, the bank is authorized, sanctions and local-market rules are satisfied, and the settlement is documented against a genuine exposure.
Spot FX conversions for operational settlement, merchant payouts, payroll, tax, and treasury rebalancing; use competitive execution, rate verification, and independent reconciliation.

Hedging instruments must not be used for unauthorized proprietary speculation. The SAS should maintain board-approved dealing authorities, ISDA or equivalent master documentation, collateral and margin procedures, counterparty limits, confirmation controls, independent valuation, derivative reporting analysis, and a documented link between each hedge and the underlying currency exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (bilan and compte de résultat) with commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 7,500 EUR, potential administrative strike-off after 3 months delay

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual tax return (liasse fiscale) with tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from 7,500 EUR plus interest, possible company dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation or within 30 days of ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR, potential criminal sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payment of corporate income tax (IS) and related declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from 7,500 EUR plus interest, possible administrative sanctions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit if annual turnover exceeds 800,000 EUR and total assets exceed 400,000 EUR
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Accounting Standards (Plan Comptable Général - PCG)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual UBO declaration or confirmation via official French registry platform with updates required within 30 days of any shareholding or control changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (art. 219 I CGI) plus 3.3% social surcharge on CIT exceeding EUR 763,000 for companies with turnover above EUR 7,630,000; reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs meeting turnover and capital criteria
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate for SMEs on the EUR 42,500 tranche; Research Tax Credit (CIR, art. 244 quater B) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20%; Young Innovative Company (JEI) social and CIT exemptions; 95% participation exemption on qualifying EU/foreign dividends (art. 145 and 216 CGI); 1-year carryback credit up to EUR 1,000,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule: Unlimited carryforward under art. 209 I CGI, subject to an annual utilisation cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; carryback limited to the preceding fiscal year up to EUR 1,000,000 (art. 220 quinquies CGI). Value 0 denotes indefinite carryforward.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_classification: Entity-level taxation without tax transparency; SAS is French tax resident when registered in France or when its effective management (siège de direction effective) is in France (art. 209 CGI)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) with annexes 2052-SD to 2059-SD; electronic filing mandatory via EFI / TéléTVA on impots.gouv.fr for all corporate taxpayers
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return plus 4 quarterly CIT instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; final balance paid with the annual return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: return due on the second business day following 1 May (andover rule); any other fiscal year end: within 3 months of closure (4 months for members of a 223 A tax consolidation group)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, SIREN, registered office, legal form, tax regime and consolidation status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate any French tax representative required under art. 164 D CGI; the SAS is the taxpayer, non-resident shareholders are not co-filers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, cash and prepaid expenses at fiscal year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capitalise payment gateway software, licences and platform intangibles at arm's length cost; intercompany receivables from the foreign parent must be priced at fair value and properly accrued

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, premiums, reserves, retained earnings, debts, provisions and accrued liabilities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose shareholder current accounts; undocumented shareholder advances from the non-resident parent may be recharacterised as hidden capital or constructive dividend

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit reconciled to taxable profit: add-backs and deductions including the 95% participation exemption and CIR
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back excessive management fees, interest and royalties paid to foreign affiliates; apply art. 238 A CGI deductibility test (real service rendered, normal price, beneficiary not in a tax haven)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065-SD / Impôt sur les sociétés dû
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT using the 15% SME tranche and 25% standard rate, 3.3% social surcharge, tax credits, instalments and balance payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SAS operates as a French permanent establishment of a foreign PSP holding an ACPR branch licence, the foreign principal files for the PE under the same rules; otherwise the SAS is autonomous

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits available for imputation: CIR, CII, foreign tax credits and withholding tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign source withholding borne by the SAS may be creditable under the relevant DTA; non-resident shareholders cannot utilise French CIR credits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of tax loss carryforwards and computation of the annual utilisation cap (EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French SAS losses cannot be used by the foreign parent absent French tax consolidation; for treaty PEs, losses are attributed under the PE profit attribution rules

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: 10% surcharge under art. 1728 CGI if no formal demand; 40% if filed within 30 days of formal demand; 80% thereafter or for organised fraud; 40% penalty for deliberate inaccuracy (manquement délibéré, art. 1729); monthly late-payment interest 0.20%; box-by-box daily fine under art. 1731 bis; minimum EUR 150 fine when no tax is due; criminal fines for wilful non-filing up to EUR 5,000

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders (art. 119 bis 2 CGI); 12.8% for non-resident individuals within the 30% flat tax (PFU, art. 200 A CGI); additional 3% levy on distributions to non-residents (art. 235 ter ZCA CGI) unless treaty-relieved
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must (i) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the competent foreign tax authority, (ii) deliver the TRC, ownership evidence and Form 5000/5001 affidavit to the paying French SAS before the dividend record date, and (iii) have the paying entity withhold at the applicable treaty rate (commonly 0%, 5% or 15%); where excess withholding occurred, claim a refund through Form 2000 before expiry of the statutory period (in principle 31 December of the second year following payment); the tax administration may re-audit treaty eligibility under the principal purpose test and beneficial ownership analysis
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a French debtor to non-residents: statutory WHT 25% (art. 182 B CGI), reduced by DTA to typically 0% or 5%; interest paid to non-residents: domestic law generally imposes no source WHT on interest paid by French companies, except 25% where the creditor is in a tax haven or controlling shareholder under art. 212 CGI and art. 119 quater CGI; treaty rates for interest typically 0%, 10% or 15%; deductibility denied under art. 238 A CGI for payments to tax-haven residents lacking genuine economic substance; reporting obligations under art. 242 ter CGI

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000: full Local File and Master File documentation required under art. L. 13 AA and L. 13 AB LPF for entities with annual turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or whose group exceeds EUR 750 million consolidated turnover; failure to produce documentation permits the administration to reconstruct profits and apply a 5% penalty on the recomputed amount (art. L. 13 B LPF)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France is not an ESR jurisdiction stricto sensu, but substance is legally enforced through: (i) effective-management residence test (art. 209 CGI); (ii) abuse-of-law recharacterisation (art. L. 64 LPF); (iii) acte anormal de gestion doctrine denying deductions for expenses failing the corporate interest test; (iv) art. 238 A CGI for payments to low-tax jurisdictions; (v) the mandatory ACPR authorisation under art. L. 522-1 C. mon. fin. (PSD2) requiring the French PSP to maintain adequate human, material and AML/KYC substance in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing merchant acquiring and clearing fees, inflating deductible charges, or re-routing French-source payment fees to the foreign parent as fictitious services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% penalty for manquement délibéré and 80% for organised fraud (art. 1729 CGI); late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (art. 1741 CGI), increased to EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years when committed through a tax-haven shelter (art. 1741-1 CGI)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and directors may be jointly and severally liable for the SAS tax debt where fraud is proven (art. L. 267 LPF); parallel criminal measures include asset freezes, confiscation, travel bans (interdiction de quitter le territoire), posting of judicial sureties, and disqualification from management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the cross-border payment gateway, merchant acquiring or clearing services on Visa, Mastercard or Fedwire rails without the ACPR licence / agrément required under art. L. 522-1 C. mon. fin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. L. 572-1 C. mon. fin.: 7 years imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine for unauthorised provision of payment services; confiscation of assets derived from the offence; public sanction; corporate fine for the SAS up to EUR 3,750,000 as the 5x multiplier under art. 131-38 Penal Code
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who implement or tolerate the unauthorised activity face the same criminal penalties; travel bans and prohibition from professional activity up to 5 years under art. L. 572-2 C. mon. fin.; personal ACPR sanctions of up to EUR 5,000,000 and loss of fitness-and-propriety for banking licences

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Structure / Abuse of Law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SAS as a letterbox with no board meetings, employees, equipment or decision-making in France, solely to exploit the French SIREN, DTA network and EU passporting, while profits are shifted to a zero-tax jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse of law (art. L. 64 LPF): 80% penalty of additional tax (40% where abuse is not established but the position is abusive), plus 0.20% monthly interest; recharacterisation of the SAS as non-resident if the actual place of management is abroad; denial of deductions under art. 238 A CGI; reassessments of 25% dividend WHT and the 3% levy
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The administration may pursue de facto managers under art. L. 267 LPF solidarity liability; criminal exposure for complicity in tax evasion; passport blocking and travel restrictions pending assessment; personal confiscation of funds channelled through the shell entity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/KYC Breach in the Cross-Border Corridor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-risk merchant flows without customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, transaction screening, or TRACFIN declarations within the statutory deadlines of art. L. 561-5 C. mon. fin.; facilitating money-mule or shell-merchant transfers over Visa/Mastercard/Fedwire rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACPR sanctions: warning, reprimand, licence suspension, fine up to EUR 100 million or 10% of annual turnover (art. L. 612-41 C. mon. fin.); money laundering offence under art. L. 465-1 C. mon. fin.: 5 years imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine, increased to 10 years and EUR 750,000 for aggravated organised laundering; ministerial asset-freezing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and the AML/COO face criminal liability for deliberate failure to implement AML controls; permanent or temporary prohibition from exercising the profession; confiscation of personal property; travel bans during the criminal investigation; adverse EBA notification may terminate EU passporting rights across other member states
